transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman. No King's protesters marched to the steps
of the Lincoln Memorial Saturday and Pierre's Ava Berger was there.
At the steps of the Lincoln Memorial, a large inflatable donkey bounced around next to a paper
mache replica of Donald Trump's head. Both were among the crowd of No King's protesters.
Inside the donkey costume was Athena Hairsine, a horse trainer from Maryland.
The front of the costume said, "Donkeys against tyranny."
I ran out of real estate on the regular sign, so I needed a way to express
all the things that I'm upset about. The No King's protest was different than the last three.
The goal, organizers say, was a non-partisan push to get the most early voters to the polls
in midterm election history. Hairsine, a registered Democrat, says it will be her
first time voting in the midterms. Ava Berger, NPR News, Washington.
A historic town hall in France that was more than 140 years old caught fire Saturday,
the incident cast a shadow on what were mostly peaceful student protests across the country,
and Pierre's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
The main protest march in Paris was peaceful, but all around were pockets of violence that
police were unable to control. 65-year-old protester Pascal Ordeux came out to march
in support of his daughter, a teacher, and his grandkids, who are students.
He says the media loves to show the violence.
It's nothing compared to what people are fighting for, he says,
and focusing on it lets the government off the hook. But TV footage showed a different story.
Some 1,200 people have been arrested and hooded youths clashed with police well into the evening.
Far left leaders who joined the protesters distanced themselves from the violence,
saying a legitimate march had been infiltrated by troublemakers.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
A man and a six-year-old boy were killed Saturday and 11 others injured when a truck
drove through a crowd of people at a soccer tournament of the youth sports complex in
Wichita, Kansas. Roger Noemmer from member station KMUW reports.
Police say they are still trying to piece together why a woman with two kids in her truck
allegedly drove through a field where children were playing soccer.
Wichita City Councilmember Becky Tuttle says she feels for the families and onlookers.
My heart breaks not only for the people that were personally impacted,
but anybody who maybe observed the horrible tragedy that happened today.
Wichita Police Captain Aaron Moses says the driver of the truck is in custody
and cooperating with authorities.
We have a really good idea of what happened. What we're working to do now
is do the investigation to determine how it happened and why.
Officials are asking anyone with video or photos from the incident to share them with police.
For NPR News, I'm Roger Noemmer in Wichita.
And this is NPR News.
Wall Street investors are bracing for earnings from major companies like
Netflix and Meta this week. NPR's Rafael Nam has our preview.
In a week that's light in terms of economic data, the quarterly earnings reports should
provide investors a good sense of how some companies are faring in an uncertain economy.
Netflix, for example, has recently announced layoffs amid concerns about whether the company
can continue to keep its subscribers spending significant time on its platform.
Meanwhile, Meta is releasing earnings amid rising concerns about whether the massive
investments in AI will pay off. And Tesla is set to report how many deliveries
it accomplished in the latest quarter, a key metric of demand for the company's vehicles.
Rafael Nam, NPR News.
Officials in Canada say an incident at a military base in Alberta this weekend
caused a fire and killed or injured a number of people.
They're not saying what the incident was or exactly how many people have been affected.
The base, which is located near the town of Wainwright, is a major training facility for
Canada's armed forces, an investigation that is being described as very active and delicate as
ongoing. A fire Saturday destroyed a beach resort in southeastern Bangladesh. At least
10 people were killed and four others were injured in the fire. The blaze broke out at
the resort in the popular tourist destination, known as Cox's Bazaar. Officials say the fire
moved quickly through the three-story wooden building. Women and children were included
among the victims. I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: No Kings protesters march to the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, emphasizing early midterm voting
Violence erupts at Paris protests, with about 1,200 arrested and a historic French town hall burned
Truck drives into children at a soccer tournament in Wichita, Kansas, killing a man and a six-year-old boy
Wall Street awaits this week's earnings reports from Netflix, Meta, and Tesla
Fire at a Canadian military training base in Alberta kills or injures several people, cause unclear
Fire destroys a beach resort in Cox's Bazaar, Bangladesh, killing at least 10 people
